dialogues.speaker: Sekkura
dialogues.text: Workload has been lighter with more dusk birds, but now that I need to take care of them, I also don't get to go home as often.

dialogues.speaker: Sekkura
dialogues.text: Dusk birds are usually used to carry messages. They're essential for my job as a Swallow Messenger.

dialogues.speaker: Sekkura
dialogues.text: While they've cut down on the need for me to run errands, I now spend a lot more time in town.

dialogues.speaker: Sekkura
dialogues.text: My home is Aaru Village, which is a small settlement on the desert edge.

dialogues.speaker: Sekkura
dialogues.text: How I long to visit Aaru Village again... It feels like an eternity since I saw Candace. We've got a lot to catch up on.

dialogues.speaker: Sekkura
dialogues.text: Such as life in the city, stories about the rainforest, and Parchamdar Rukh Shah...

dialogues.speaker: Sekkura
dialogues.text: Rukh Shah is not only dependable, he's the youngest Parchamdar in Corps history!

dialogues.speaker: Sekkura
dialogues.text: Supposedly he's from the rainforest, not the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Sekkura
dialogues.text: You know how rare rainforest people are in the ranks of the Eremites, much less a Parchamdar.

dialogues.speaker: Sekkura
dialogues.text: He's very impressive, getting along not only with the desert dwellers, but Akademiya researchers too.

dialogues.speaker: Sekkura
dialogues.text: Maybe there's truth to the rumor that he was once a researcher himself.
